text.text_excerpt: I love this place. I'm a honky simpleton and admittedly could be more adventurous about what I eat. I have the palate of a cavechild. Before moving to New Orleans, I never even knew what a Banh Mi was. Now that I do, I'm infatuated with them, and these are the best I've had. Admittedly, I haven't globe trotted looking for the perfect Vietnamese sandwich, but I don't need to to know these are damn good. The bread is light and flaky and the ingredients are always fresh. The service is super-friendly and quick. The prices are outrageously cheap. My only caveat is that it's so damn far away. I live in uptown, so it's quite a trek. But that should tell you something right there.

Really good Banh Mi's (vietnamese sandwiches) here, and they are really cheap. Had the shredded pork, which is a marinated (roasted?) pork sliced up. They do not put cilantro in their sandwiches which is great for me cuz i dont like it. They never use frozen meat. Always fresh. Also had their combination (meatball & shredded pork) and their specialty (meatball, shredded pork, and asian ham). All were prety good but i really love the specialty. Their meatball is not the chewy (and i think not tasty) meatballs you get in your pho. Its more like your traditional meatballs. Meatball sandwich gets a 3 out of 5. All sandwiches were $3 with the exception of the specialty, which is $4. Unbelievea...

I crave these all the time. The combination with the meatballs and the shredded pork, topped off with pickled carrots and radish, is so amazing. Get it spicy; they make their own chili paste (aka homemade Sriracha status). The french bread is lightly toasted but still soft and slightly chewy inside. All my friends like to reminisce about how they would sell banh mi from the window of their house. Cash only and they close really early, at like 4:30 or 4, depending on when they feel like it, I guess. You can also buy a ceramic Mary statue, candy, or a plant in a ceramic pot here.
